question: Should OpenClaw accept a core operational-notice routing policy with durable once-state and fail-closed operator-session redirect, and what recovery guarantee should apply when the redirect write fails?
rationale: This is a public configuration and message-privacy boundary spanning core delivery, plugin hooks, and persisted state; code review cannot choose the desired disclosure-versus-observability tradeoff.

options.title: Approve a bounded core policy
options.body: Keep the compatible always default, document the redirect-failure recovery contract, and require focused upgrade and affected-channel proof before landing.

options.title: Split the immediate leak repair
options.body: Land a narrower fix for the confirmed fallback-notice leak while deferring once and redirect semantics to a separately approved design.

options.title: Keep policy ownership outside core
options.body: Reject the broad core surface if maintainers determine existing generic delivery contracts should not own operational-notice routing.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded core policy
recommendation.body: Keep the compatible always default, document the redirect-failure recovery contract, and require focused upgrade and affected-channel proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the recent core reply-delivery, ACP, plugin SDK, and configuration paths tied to this proposal.
